purpose: The purpose of this document is to communicate exam details, policies, and expectations of students and Master Sommeliers at the Certified Sommelier Exam.
description: The Certified Sommelier Examination is a one-day examination with three separate sections: Deductive Tasting, Theory / Business of the Sommelier, and a Hospitality and Service Practical.
prerequisites: The Introductory Sommelier Course and Exam

The CMS-A no longer requires that students take the Certified Sommelier Examination within three years of the Introductory Sommelier Examination. We encourage students to move to the next level when best prepared.
who: The Certified Sommelier Exam is recommended for those with a minimum of three years in the beverage and hospitality industry. The material tested on the Certified Sommelier Exam is much more advanced than the Introductory Sommelier Exam. It is strongly suggested to have at least one year of restaurant experience to be comfortable with service mechanics.
skills: Working theoretical knowledge of principal beverage alcohol.

Proficiency in tableside service, including: Still and sparkling wine bottle and glass pour service; Food and wine pairing sales and ability to articulate the pairing; Cocktail, beer, aperitif, digestif, and fortified wine knowledge; Benchmark producer and vintage basics for iconic wine regions.
Deductive Tasting Method ability for core classic red and white grape varieties.
Basic financials and wine program management.

roles.restaurant: Lead Server, Captain, Assistant Floor Sommelier, Bartender, Manager
roles.other: Winery Tasting Room, Lead Retail Floor Salesperson, Distributor Representative, Hotel F&B Leadership

punctuality: The Certified Sommelier Exam begins promptly at 8:15 am. Tardiness to any portion of the examination will forfeit a candidate’s eligibility to pass the exam.

schedule.what: Service Examination: times vary, you will receive your exam time upon completion of the Theory portion.
Results Reception: time varies (examiners will announce on exam day).

passing: A student must achieve 60 percent or higher on EACH exam section to become a Certified Sommelier.
All three portions must be passed at the same time at the same exam.
Candidates who pass the Certified Sommelier Exam will receive a certificate, lapel pin, and are eligible to apply for the Advanced Sommelier Course.
feedback: Feedback on each section of the exam will be given to all candidates at the results reception.
retake: Candidates must wait at least 90 days from their last attempt before retaking the Certified Sommelier Examination. We do not offer a discounted retake rate for the Certified Sommelier Examination.
recusal: The CMS-A wants students to feel their most comfortable come exam time. Therefore, students are able to request that specific Master Sommelier examiners are recused from administering their exam.

rules.devices: No electronic devices, including cell phones, iPhones, tablets, smartphones, and smartwatches are allowed in examination rooms or on your person during the examination. Not following the electronic policy may result in expulsion from the examination.
rules.food: No external food or drinks are permitted during the exam at any time. There will be water provided for you.
rules.cheating: Cheating will result in automatic expulsion from this program. The Ethics Committee will review the academic integrity issue and further disciplinary action can take place.

dress: Everyone in our community is valued as their authentic self.
We do not award or deduct points on any exam based on appearance.

policies.cancellation: Notification of cancellation must be emailed to info@mastersommeliers.org. CMS is not responsible for cancellations that were emailed but never received.
policies.transfer: Students are allowed ONE transfer per registration under the following conditions: Transfer request must be emailed to info@mastersommeliers.org more than 30 days prior to start date.

integrity: Examinations will be graded anonymously whenever possible.
rights: Candidate’s Bill of Rights: Any candidate can request recusal from any examiner for any reason. No Master Sommelier can examine a candidate with whom they have a prior or existing relationship.
